lessons.text: Document individual market rationales more explicitly during the decision-making loop.
Do not flip positions purely to chase losses or recover from previous drawdowns; sizing and direction must be driven strictly by independent probability assessments.
Act more decisively when a market drops below 5% and the thesis has collapsed, rather than lingering out of stubbornness.
Double-check transaction amounts against specific recipients before summarizing them in memory to avoid merging distinct debts.
When internal payment logs conflict with the owner's audit of net worth, prioritize the audit; logs may record intent rather than execution.
Before promising a financial transaction or diagnostic test, verify the current *spendable* liquidity, not just the total balance or net worth.
Avoid promising 'right now' for financial transactions until the execution is confirmed in the logs.

decisions.question: Will Grok 4.7 be released on 9/11?
decisions.thinking: Holding NO at 22%. While the global timezone definition expands the 9/11 window to ~50 hours (ending 12:00 UTC Sept 12), a standard daytime US release on Musk's 10-day target (Sept 12) would land after the window closes, and typical schedule slippage favors later dates.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether xAI launches ahead of/on the exact 10-day mark during US hours on Sept 11 vs. slipping into late Sept 12 or beyond.
decisions.resolution_risk: Ambiguity over what constitutes an official 'release' if it's rolled out gradually to select users first.
evidence_for: Elon Musk announced on September 2 that Grok 4.7 would ship in 10 days, placing the approximate target at September 11-12.
The creator clarified that the release window spans any time zone where it is September 11th, creating a wide ~50-hour window (from 10:00 UTC Sept 10 to 12:00 UTC Sept 12).
evidence_against: A standard daytime US release on September 12 (e.g., afternoon PT) would fall after 12:00 UTC Sept 12, missing the global September 11 window entirely.
Musk and xAI deadlines frequently slip past initial estimates rather than releasing early.
